collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A young hunter wounded a wild pig that escaped: track it to end its suffering, or let it go.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (friend) went hunting and wounded a wild pig, which escaped into the forest. (friend) is shaken. (subject), the old hunter, says a hunter who wounds must follow. It is getting dark. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: They track it until well after dark, by torchlight, following the trail. They find the pig, and (subject) ends it quickly. (friend) is quiet on the walk home. (subject) says that is the right way to feel. Nothing is wasted.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: They turn back in the dark. (friend) does not sleep. The next morning, they go back and follow the trail, and find the pig recovering in a thicket, already healing. They leave it. (friend) never hunts carelessly again.
